overall: The AG found the Newburyport City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by posting its October 15, 2024 meeting notice late, counting the October 14 holiday. The amendment allegation was not reached. No further remedy was ordered because minutes and video are public and nullification was not sought.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council failed to post notice 48 hours before its October 15, 2024 meeting, with the holiday on October 14 at issue.
allegations.key_passage: Because Monday, October 14, was a legal holiday in Massachusetts, we find that notice of the Council’s October 15 meeting was not posted 48 hours, excluding weekends and holidays, in advance of the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council improperly amended the October 15, 2024 notice within 48 hours of the meeting to add a previously anticipated topic.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find that the meeting notice was not timely posted in the first instance

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
